node.label: Franca Iacovetta
node.date_label: Such Hardworking People (1992) · Enemies Within (co-edited with Roberto Perin and Angelo Principe) (2000) · Gatekeepers (2006)
node.description: A Canadian historian of gender, migration and class. Gatekeepers investigates how everyday institutions tried to reshape newcomers in Cold War Canada, while keeping immigrant responses and inequalities in view. Her editorial collaborations retain their joint credit.

proposed_edges.relationship: Examines everyday gatekeeping and the contested remaking of immigrant citizenship in Cold War Canada.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Basok and Bastable’s substantive reading of Gatekeepers supports this scoped claim, including immigrant negotiation/resistance; it is not full-book verification.

proposed_edges.relationship: Places gendered expectations about marriage, family and sexuality inside the regulation of newcomers.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: The same review’s treatment of Gatekeepers makes these mechanisms substantive, rather than inferring a gender arrow from Iacovetta’s appointment.
